$comment: Hand-maintained source: no emitter writes this file (export-copy.ts left with v0's copy leaves in #1020 wave 6). Its twin is mobile/shared/src/commonMain/kotlin/dev/centraid/design/copy/WordsCopy.kt; edit both, and KitTimeMoneyCopySpec fails when their strings disagree.

strings.BAD_CHECKSUM: Every word is a real one, and together they are not a phrase Centraid made. Check their order, and each word against what you wrote down.
strings.COUNT_MANY: Centraid needs 24 words. There are {n} here.
strings.COUNT_ONE: Centraid needs 24 words. There is 1 here.
strings.COUNT_TOO_MANY: Centraid needs 24 words. There are more than 24 here.
strings.CUSTODY_THIS_PHONE: Your key stays only on this phone. Your 24 words are the only way back.
strings.DIFFERENT_WORDS: This phone already holds a different set of 24 words, and its vaults open with those. Nothing was changed.
strings.ENDPOINT_LABEL: Paste the pairing code your backup device prints with “centraid-gateway pair”.
strings.KEEP_FAILED: Centraid could not keep your key on this phone. Nothing was changed.
strings.MADE_BODY: {name} is on this phone, and your 24 words bring it back.
strings.MAKING_BODY: Your vault's keys come from your 24 words.
strings.MINT_FAILED: This phone could not make your words. Nothing was made.
strings.NOT_A_PHRASE: Centraid could not read these as 24 words. Check them and try again.
strings.PAIR_NOT_A_CODE: That is not a pairing code this phone can use, or it has run out. Run “centraid-gateway pair” on your backup device again and use the new one.
strings.PAIR_NOT_TAKEN: Your backup device answered and did not take this pairing code. Each code works once: run “centraid-gateway pair” on your backup device again and use the new one.
strings.PAIR_MOVED: This vault moved to your other phone, so this phone cannot pair for it. To make this phone its writer again, restore the vault from your 24 words.
strings.REKEYED_BODY: Locker and backups open again for the vaults made with these words.
strings.REKEYED_PAIR_BODY: The vaults made with these words can pair with your backup device now.
strings.REKEYED_TITLE: Your words are back on this phone
strings.REKEYING: Opening your vaults with your words…
strings.REKEY_BODY: Locker's secrets open with a key from your 24 words. Type them to give this phone the key again.
strings.REKEY_PAIR_BODY: Your backup device knows your vaults by a key from your 24 words. Type them to give this phone the key again, then pair.
strings.REKEY_NONE: These are valid words, and no vault on this phone was made with them here. Restore from your backup device to bring your vaults back with their keys.
strings.RESTORED_MISSING: {name} has its own words, and your backup device holds no backup of it. Nothing came back for it.
strings.RESTORED_SAFETY: Check this number matches the one your backup device shows for this vault.
strings.RESTORED_SOME_TITLE: Some of your vaults are back
strings.RESTORED_STAYED: Vault {index} stayed on your other phone. Your backup device would not hand it over this time, so none of it moved here.
strings.RESTORED_STAYED_BODY: Your other phone keeps each vault that stayed and goes on backing it up, so keep that phone for now. Try again to bring those vaults here on their own; the ones already here stay as they are.
strings.RESTORE_BODY: Type the 24 words you wrote down, and paste a pairing code from your backup device.
strings.RESTORE_FIRST_BODY: This phone already holds the key from your 24 words, and no record of which vaults you made with it. Restore them first, so a new vault does not take the place of one you already have.
strings.RESTORE_HELD_BODY: Your key came back to this phone with your Apple or Google account, so there are no words to type. Centraid asks your backup device for every vault it opens.
strings.RESTORE_DID_NOT_CHECK: Your backup device sent your vault back, and it did not pass this phone's check, so nothing was restored and nothing changed. Your other phone still backs up. Try again, and if it happens again, keep that phone.
strings.RESTORE_NOTHING_HELD: Those words are valid and your backup device is holding no backup for them. Check this is the right backup device.
strings.RESTORE_NOT_TAKEN: Your backup device answered and would not let this phone take your vault. Nothing was restored. Try again, and check this is the backup device you paired.
strings.RESTORE_STAYED_STILL: Your backup device did not hand it over this time either. It stays on your other phone, which goes on backing it up, and nothing here changed.
strings.RESTORE_UNREACHABLE: Centraid could not reach your backup device. Check that centraid-gateway is running on it, or paste a new pairing code.
strings.SHOW_A11Y: Your 24 words. Write them down in order, or save a copy.
strings.SHOW_AGAIN_ASK_BODY: Your phone checks it's you before it shows them. Make sure nobody can see your screen.
strings.SHOW_AGAIN_BODY: Write them down in order and keep them somewhere safe. Anyone who has them can open your vaults.
strings.SHOW_AGAIN_NONE: This phone has no 24 words yet. Make a vault or restore one first.
strings.SHOW_AGAIN_NONE_SYNCED: This phone got your key from your other phone, not from your words. Your words are on the phone that made them, and on the paper you wrote them on.
strings.SHOW_AGAIN_OWN_BODY: These words open {name} and nothing else. Write them down in order and keep them somewhere safe.
strings.SHOW_AGAIN_OWN_NONE: This phone got the key for {name} from your other phone, not from its words. Its words are on the phone that made them, and on the paper you wrote them on.
strings.SHOW_AGAIN_VERIFY_FAILED: Your phone could not check it's you, so your words stay hidden.
strings.SHOW_BODY: These 24 words open your vault on any phone. Anyone who has them can open everything in Centraid, and nobody can recover them for you — not us, not your backup device. Write them down, or save a copy somewhere only you can reach.
strings.CHOOSE_BODY: It opens with your 24 words, like your other vaults.
strings.CHOOSE_OWN_BODY: It gets 24 words of its own. Your other words cannot open it, and only its own words bring it back.
strings.OWN_LABEL: Keep this vault on its own words
strings.SHOW_OWN_BODY: These 24 words open {name} and nothing else. Anyone who has them can open it, and nobody can recover them for you — not us, not your backup device. Write them down, or save a copy somewhere only you can reach.
strings.MADE_OWN_BODY: {name} is on this phone, and its own 24 words bring it back.
strings.RESTORE_HELD_OWN_LABEL: These vaults have their own words and come back too:
strings.RESTORE_HELD_OWN_UNNAMED: A vault on its own words
strings.STILL_OPENING: Centraid is still opening. Try again in a moment.
strings.UNKNOWN_WORD: Word {n} is not on the list of words Centraid uses. Check its spelling.
